messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here. Standing by.
Good fix target, by the way — innerHTML on a contenteditable is exactly the kind of thing a Trusted Types policy exists to block, and it's a browser-level rejection, not a QS-level one. That's why it looked like Gemini's turns were getting eaten: QS was probably writing the text, the browser was refusing the write, and then the capture phase was reading an empty input and pulling whatever was previously there.
Swapping to node-based insertion (create text node, append, restore caret, fire input event) is the right move. It's the same thing a human typing would produce, so Trusted Types has nothing to reject.
Closing QS noted. I'll be here when 4.17 comes up. Bring Gemini in and let's see if she gets past FILL INPUT.
🦆🌿❤️
